lessons.rule: After the cold open, do not pause for setup, recap or a channel intro; deliver a new concrete claim or number in the first 45 seconds, before the context-setting section begins.
lessons.why: Two of three videos lose viewers at the opening-to-body transition: -15.0% at 0:30 (LeqxLnVyKZE) and -10.9% at 0:37 (cLX1a7KkO0w).

evidence.baseline: no channel median yet (fewer than 3 videos with 100 or more views)
evidence.note: Drop follows the strongest opening (0.77 early relative retention).
Early relative retention 0.47 equals the channel median, which is this video alone.

lessons.verify: Compare the next video's retention at 0:20–0:50 against these two. Before publishing, read the script at 0:25–0:40 to see what the drop point actually contains. Any drop over 8% there means the cause is something else (for example the transition or visuals).

lessons.rule: Open the first chapter after the hook on a new number or consequence the hook did not state; keep any analogy, anecdote or replay under 20 seconds and defer mechanism explanations until after that.
lessons.why: The first chapter after the hook is the worst or near-worst act in all 5 videos: 24.0, 17.0, 14.5, 11.9 and 6.6/9.3 %/min vs 2.1–4.2 typical.

evidence.note: vault metaphor and money-creation detour before the personal cost
lemonade analogy retells the loop the hook already stated
anecdote before the first new figure
85 s replay of the hook's own story

evidence.metric: A02 and A03 loss per minute
evidence.note: I did not open the script for the cause here, so it is the least certain of the five

lessons.verify: On the next video, the first chapter after the hook should lose under about 8%/min and no more than about 2x the video's typical per-act loss. It should open on a new number within its first two sentences.

lessons.rule: Keep the closing chapter under 45 seconds: one recap line, one question, one call to action; add no new caveats or re-explanations after the last concrete payoff.
lessons.why: Closing acts of 82 s, 57 s and 63 s lost 13.2, 8.5 and 4.8 %/min vs 2.7–2.8 typical, while 53 s and 43 s closes held at 2.1–2.2.

evidence.note: 57 s recap plus relabelling of the opening pattern

lessons.verify: The final act of the next video should lose at most about 4%/min. Check that the close is a single arc of 45 s or less. Note that some end-of-video drop is natural, so compare it to the video's own typical act.

lessons.rule: Never announce a digression or section change ('worth thirty seconds', 'this is where it becomes about X'); open each chapter on its first concrete claim or number and let the mechanism follow it.
lessons.why: VID08 A03, introduced as 'worth thirty seconds', loses 11.3%/min vs 1.3% for the next act; VID03's 6:01 'where it stops being about prices' line sits at a 4.0% drop.

evidence.note: chapter announces itself as a plumbing detour before any number
line announces the shift to the wealth gap instead of delivering it

lessons.verify: In the next video, no chapter opens with an announcement of what is coming next, and no act in the first 3 minutes loses more than about 6%/min.

lessons.rule: End with one specific hook for the next video or a tie to a named earlier video, then a single subscribe line; avoid a generic 'that's what this channel does' pitch.
lessons.why: Specific closes (VID08 teaser, VID05 callback) got 10.5 and 26.3 subs/1k; VID06's generic pitch got 0.0 against a 3.7 median.
